title: finance/customers
description: One row per banking customer. Individuals who hold accounts. Accounts, cards and loans all point back here, so this is the table to start from when exploring the topic.

id.description: Surrogate primary key, sequential from 1. Use this for joins rather than the national identifier.

customer_number.description: The bank's own reference for this person, quoted on correspondence and in the branch.

full_name.description: Spanish name carrying both surnames, the father's followed by the mother's. Worth testing any name-parsing code against.

national_id.description: Spanish DNI: eight digits and a check letter derived modulo 23. Structurally valid, so it passes a real DNI validator, but registered to nobody.

birth_date.description: Date of birth. Customers are between 18 and 92, following a realistic adult population shape rather than a flat spread.

email.description: Contact address on the reserved example.com domain, with accents transliterated. Empty for about 7% of customers.

phone.description: Mobile number in Spanish format. Banks require a contact number for two-factor authentication, so unlike email this column is never empty.

city.description: Spanish city of residence, usually but not always the city of the branch where the account was opened.

province.description: Province of residence, consistent with the postal code that follows it.

postal_code.description: Spanish postal code whose first two digits are the province code, so the two columns always agree.

kyc_status.description: Know Your Customer verification state. Regulators require banks to confirm identity; the 14% who are pending or expired are the rows a compliance screen should surface.

risk_score.description: Internal credit and fraud risk rating from 1 to 100, where higher is riskier. Correlates inversely with income, so a scatter plot of the two slopes downward.

annual_income.description: Declared gross annual income in euros, following a lognormal distribution -- most customers cluster near the median with a long tail above it, as real incomes do. Empty for about 18% who never declared one.

customer_since.description: Date the relationship began, always on or before the opening date of their earliest account.
